|BearSSL
|by design: `+aes_ct64+` and `+ghash_ctmul64+`, or AES-NI and PCLMUL where the CPU has them; on a 32-bit host a 64-bit multiplication may not be constant time, which BearSSL documents; ECDSA signing with webcpp's fix, since upstream's decoding of the RFC 6979 nonce branches on its bit length (link:https://www.bearssl.org/gitweb/?p=BearSSL;a=blob;f=src/ec/ecdsa_i31_bits.c;hb=7bea48e5e850ab4cafbe68d3765cdaba13a86d6f#l44[BearSSL's ecdsa_i31_bits.c at upstream 7bea48e, lines 44 and 45: the nonce decoded with its actual bit length in the integer's header, then shifted over the words that length needs]; link:https://minerva.crocs.fi.muni.cz/[Minerva: the leak of an ECDSA nonce's bit length through timing, and the lattice that recovers the key (CVE-2019-15809)]; the fix: link:https://github.com/webcpporg/bearssl/commit/32381d6e787a32cbb7a687246349200d78b8ff7c[webcpporg/bearssl, commit 32381d6 on its branch webcpp: the header set back to the order's length before the shift, in ecdsa_i31_bits.c and ecdsa_i15_bits.c]); link:https://www.bearssl.org/constanttime.html[BearSSL, constant-time crypto]; link:https://www.bearssl.org/ctmul.html[BearSSL, constant-time multiplications]

Measured where a family differs from its backend's design:

* X25519 on libsodium, native: nothing found with arm64's DIT (data-independent timing) bit set, which webcpp sets around every call on 64-bit ARM under macOS, iOS, Linux and Android where the CPU has it, as Apple requires of constant-time code (link:https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations[Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations]); the lane's dudect sets nothing itself and measures what a program gets: |t| 1.8 to 2.8 against the threshold 10 (2026-11-21, five runs), while its `+dudect_planted+`, an early-exit scan of the secret key run inside the same guard, reads |t| 66.72 and 65.53 (2026-11-21): DIT does not hide a leak. Without DIT, dudect times `+agree+` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 6.7 to 14.5 (2026-11-19) and 4.3 to 7.8 (2026-11-21, three runs): about one nanosecond in 15 µs. Each on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build. libsodium does not set DIT, and webcpp sets nothing on x86, WebAssembly or Windows on ARM64
* X25519 on libsodium, wasip2: an open finding, its cause measured: dudect times `+agree+` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 13 to 32 (2026-11-18; a fixed key against another fixed key: 22.9) and 107 to 260 (2026-11-19), and 25.25 in the lane on 2026-11-21, against the threshold 10, under wasmtime 47 on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build. The cause is Apple silicon's DIT (data-independent timing), which wasmtime does not set (link:https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations[Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations]): with DIT set in wasmtime's main thread, an experiment and not the lane, the same case reads |t| 1.5 to 2.1; no branch on a secret was found in the WebAssembly or in wasmtime's compiled code. The lane cannot set DIT from inside the WebAssembly, so it prints this value on wasip2 without judging it; the CI's x86-64 run measures it next
